children.text: Candon Church is the parish church of Ilocos Sur dedicated to Saint John of Sahagun (San Juan de Sahagun), and its history traces back to 1591, when the Augustinians accepted Candon as a house. Its four-storey octagonal bell tower and two Rosary ceiling paintings, each about 46 m long, are the main sights.

The church's formal name is Saint John of Sahagun Parish Church, but locals simply call it Candon Church. It is a Catholic parish church in the heart of Candon City, Ilocos Sur, under the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia, and it is still an active church with regular Masses. It does not carry a World Heritage label like Vigan or Paoay, but in the middle of Candon, about
343km
north of Manila, you can see traces of the Spanish colonial period from the late 17th and early 18th centuries just as they are.

Its history goes back to 1591, when the Augustinians accepted Candon as a house; records say Father Pedro Bravo began building one of the early churches in 1695. A major earthquake in 1707 badly damaged the church, and it was rebuilt under Father Jose Carbonel until 1710 and then under Father Diego del Castillo until 1713. The architectural style that came out of rebuilding after earthquakes is commonly called Earthquake Baroque. In 2016, a national historical marker recognizing the church's historic value was unveiled.

The most eye-catching part of the exterior is the four-storey octagonal bell tower. Open and blind windows alternate, a balustrade runs around it, and a small campanile sits at the top. Because the tower is visible from almost anywhere in town, it works as a landmark when you first arrive in Candon. Inside, colorful murals and stained-glass windows fill the ceiling and walls, along with an altar covered in gold leaf. The charm of this church is that the solemnity of an old stone church and the bright colors of comparatively recent paintwork sit together.

On an itinerary, it works less as a standalone destination and more as a stopover on the way from Vigan to Laoag, or when coming up from La Union. It is a quiet town church rather than a big attraction, so one to two hours is about right for a few photos, a look at the ceiling paintings, and a taste of Candon's famous kalamay nearby. The city itself is also worth knowing. In the 2024 census, Candon had about 61,000 people and became the most populous city in Ilocos Sur. Famous for tobacco farming, it is called the tobacco capital, and in town you will find the Candon City Museum (the Cariño ancestral house), a former bahay na bato house from the 1700s, and an aquarium park that opened in 2025. Visiting these after the church fills out a full day. Opening hours and entrance fees can change, so check before you go.

An octagonal tower with alternating open and blind windows, a balustrade and a campanile at the top, it is the signature element of Earthquake Baroque style. It is Candon's landmark, visible from anywhere in town.

blocks.title: Rosary ceiling paintings, about 46 m long

children.text: Inside the church are two canvas paintings, each nearly
(150 feet) long. They depict the 20 Mysteries of the Holy Rosary and are described as the longest religious painting in the Philippines. They were unveiled in December 2007.

The ceiling and walls are filled with bright murals and stained-glass windows. A scene of the Last Supper is also said to be painted on the ceiling. The colors are most vivid when morning light comes in.
The main altar is decorated with gold leaf, giving you a taste of the ornate atmosphere typical of old Philippine stone churches. During Mass, avoid taking photos and moving around.
The church grounds have a grotto dedicated to Our Lady of Lourdes. It is a quiet spot where local worshippers light candles and pray.
A national historical marker unveiled in 2016 explains the church's historic value. Reading its text gives you a quick summary of how the church was built and rebuilt.
Along the road near city hall and the church, stalls sell Candon's famous kalamay (a chewy sweet made from glutinous rice, coconut milk and sugar). It makes a great gift to take home.

items.title: Candon half-day route
items.subtitle: From the church to town monuments and the beach

children.text: Look around the exterior of the church and its bell tower from near the town plaza. Seeing the front, the side and the tower from different angles shows the structure of the octagonal tower well.
Go inside and take your time with the Rosary ceiling paintings, murals, stained glass and the gold-leaf altar. Avoid Mass times, and move quietly if worshippers are praying.
See the Lourdes grotto and the historical marker in the grounds, then taste kalamay at the stalls in front of the church or buy some as a gift.
Visit places in town that tell Candon's modern history, such as the Sakada workers monument and the Isabelo Abaya monument. Check locations locally.
After lunch, head to Darapidap Beach and walk along the sand. You can get between the beach and town by tricycle, but confirm the fare before you ride.
If you have time left, visit the Candon City Museum, housed in the Cariño ancestral house, or the aquarium park. Check opening hours and fees locally.
If you are traveling north to Vigan (about
60km
) or south toward San Fernando, La Union, the church and kalamay stops from this route are enough.
Candon is about
343km
from Manila, and the MacArthur Highway runs through the city. Long-distance buses linking Manila, Baguio and Laoag stop in Candon.

Older sources list Partas, Dominion Bus Lines, Sta. Lucia Express, Martinez Trans and Candon Bus Line as serving Candon. Routes, departure terminals, fares and schedules change, so check each company's latest announcements.
From Manila this is usually a full day's distance, so many travelers take a night bus or stay overnight in Vigan or La Union and go on from there.
Travel time varies greatly with traffic and stops along the way, so it is safest to confirm it locally.

items.title: By car or rental car from Manila

children.text: From Manila, take NLEX and SCTEX north, then follow the MacArthur Highway through La Union into Ilocos Sur.
The route is easy to follow, but the distance is long, so build in rest stops. Parking depends on street conditions around the church, so confirm locally.
It is about
60km
from Vigan to Candon. Minibuses running between Vigan and San Fernando, La Union pass through Candon.
When getting off, tell the driver "Candon proper" or "in front of the church," and they will often let you know.

items.title: By plane and getting around town

children.text: The nearest commercial airport is Laoag International Airport (LAO) to the north. After arriving, the usual way is to take a bus south toward Candon. Flight routes change by season, so check.
Within Candon you get around by tricycle and jeepney. The church is close to the town plaza, so you can walk to it from the city hall and market area.
The dry season in Candon usually runs from October to May, with January and February the driest. August is known as the rainiest month. The average temperature is about

You can visit the church even on a rainy day, but if you also plan to cover the beach and outdoor monuments in town, November to April is best. The Tobacco Festival is held every March, and the Feria de Candon trade fair honoring Saint Barbara takes place in the first week of December. The feast day of the patron saint, Saint John of Sahagun, is June 12. During festivals the town is crowded and rooms fill up early, so check ahead.

items.note: As an active parish church it is usually not charged, but no official fee notice could be confirmed. Donations are voluntary; visit quietly during Mass

Candon has few lodgings aimed at travelers, so when Candon is a stop in the middle of a trip, many people stay in Vigan or San Fernando, La Union and travel from there. If you want to stay overnight in Candon, check the latest information and reviews on a booking app.

The food to try is definitely kalamay. It is a chewy, sweet snack made from glutinous rice, coconut milk and sugar, and Candon is known for large, hefty kalamay. You can easily buy it from the roadside stalls near the church and city hall, so pick some up as a gift for the trip home. In the market you can also try meals typical of the Ilocos region.
Many worshippers attend Mass, so avoiding those times lets you view the ceiling paintings quietly. Check the parish announcements or the church's social media for Mass times.
Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees is safer than shorts or sleeveless tops.
You look up at the ceiling paintings with your head tilted back, so viewing them slowly, one panel at a time, makes the 20 mysteries easier to tell apart.
The colors are best when morning sun passes through the stained glass, so it is best to visit in the morning.
Kalamay stalls differ in size and packaging, so compare one or two before you buy.
Follow the posted rules inside the church on photography, and do not use flash during Mass.
Because this is a long trip along the MacArthur Highway, combining it with Vigan and La Union on one itinerary reduces wasted travel.
Candon is famous for tobacco farming, so there are many street events during the March Tobacco Festival. Join in if your schedule fits.
For the exterior, shooting from the plaza side gets the bell tower in a single frame. In the afternoon the light tends to be behind it.
Candon Church is a working church where worshippers still attend Mass. Keep quiet during Mass and prayer times, and refrain from taking photos.
Bus routes, fares and departure times change often, so check each company's latest announcements before you travel.
We could not confirm the church's opening hours or Mass times for this guide. Check locally.
Agree on the fare before boarding a tricycle or buying from a market stall.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons, heavy rain can make road conditions worse, so check the weather forecast.
During holidays and festivals the town is crowded and rooms fill up early.
